summary: What: Project S.P.H.E.R.E. (Spatial Positioning Harmonic Empirical Resonance Experiment) is an independent, pre-launch research proposal.
Question: does moving a hollow copper sphere produce a reproducible change in its resonant frequency once ordinary environmental effects are accounted for?
Status: proposal stage. There are no measurement results, and the locational-variable idea is a hypothesis, not established physics.
Where to start: the LOC-1 draft protocol, the whitepaper and the FAQ.
Project S.P.H.E.R.E. is an open, independent research initiative proposing a controlled test of a locational-variable hypothesis.
The proposed test uses a hollow copper sphere and one mechanical resonance above 230 kHz; this band is a proposal, not a validated threshold.
Nothing here is a result. Claims are framed as hypotheses, plans and drafts until independent review and replication exist.
LOC-1 is a draft same-laboratory pilot design comparing a moved test sphere with a fixed reference.
It is not a completed experiment and not an issued preregistration; no public OSF registration exists yet.
A null result would set an upper bound under the tested conditions; any unexpected signal would first need artifact checks and independent replication.
SPHEREVL (the Control Room) is an educational simulation of the S.P.H.E.R.E. measurement laboratory.
It does not contain measurements and is not scientific validation of the hypothesis.
The page lists the public repository facts and development history behind the simulator.

faqs.question: Does SPHEREVL show real measurements?
faqs.answer: No. SPHEREVL is an educational simulation of the proposed laboratory workflow. It displays simulated data and is not a record of measurements or scientific validation.

faqs.question: Can SPHEREVL confirm the locational-variable hypothesis?
faqs.answer: No. A simulator cannot confirm a physical hypothesis. Only a qualified, reviewed and independently replicated measurement could do that, and none has been performed.

summary: This hub lists proposed research pages on synchronized copper-sphere frequency measurement.
Topics include error budgets, protocols, hardware, record-and-replay tests and verification.
The synchronized-measurement pages do not amend the LOC-1 draft protocol.
Version 1.0 whitepaper: open resonance metrology, digital-twin validation and accountable research funding.
It is a proposal document. It reports no measurements and no funding totals.
Read it together with the LOC-1 draft protocol.
